\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

We formalized recursive generation depth estimation and showed that a compact feature set dominated by perplexity tail statistics achieves 70--85\% four-class accuracy ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$), with five features sufficing for 97.6\% of full performance and classifier-agnostic convergence within $\leq$0.4pp.
The dominant pair (\texttt{p90\_ppl} top-2 in 9/9 cells, \texttt{var\_surprisal} in 8/9 under SHAP) generalizes across model families without retraining, making depth estimation a measurable early warning for model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}.

Cross-strategy transfer remains the primary bottleneck (59.1\% vs.\ 66.4\% cross-model), with the temperature-induced d1/d2 AUC inversion making single-classifier deployment across unknown decoding strategies infeasible.
A two-stage pipeline---first identifying the decoding strategy, then applying a strategy-conditioned depth classifier---could address this, though automating strategy identification from text alone requires independent validation.
Depth-graduated data curation is conceptually enabled by our method, but the d1/d2 boundary reversal and 26.8--52.6\% d2 recall in transfer settings preclude direct deployment without strategy metadata or a reliable strategy-identification front-end.
Real-world documents may also interleave passages at mixed recursive depths within a single document; our passage-level classifier assumes uniform depth, and extending to segment-level estimation introduces a granularity--statistical-power tradeoff that remains unexplored.
Web-crawl deployment requires model-specific calibration (C4 FPR: 4.7--22.4\%; Table~\ref{tab:calibration}), and all experiments use 1--1.5B models.
Future work should validate on mixed-domain corpora at larger scales and evaluate whether depth-graduated curation, with appropriate strategy conditioning, improves downstream training outcomes.

\section{The Depth Degradation Atlas}
\label{sec:atlas}

We present the Depth Degradation Atlas: a systematic empirical map of how statistical fingerprints evolve across recursive generation depths, models, and decoding strategies.
The atlas spans $3 \times 3 = 9$ model--strategy cells evaluated at depths $d \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, with depth extensions to $d{=}5$ for cross-model EDD validation (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).

%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{In-Distribution Performance}
\label{sec:atlas:id}

Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} reports four-class Random Forest accuracy (5-fold CV, 200 trees) across all nine cells.
Accuracy ranges from 69.6\% (Pythia, top-$k$) to 85.4\% (GPT-2~XL, temperature), all exceeding the 25\% chance baseline by a wide margin.
Two axis effects emerge.
GPT-2~XL achieves the highest accuracy under every strategy (76.6--85.4\%), followed by OLMo (74.2--82.0\%) and Pythia (69.6--78.2\%).
Top-$k$ sampling yields the lowest accuracy in every model.
The mean within-model strategy gap is 8.4~pp, comparable to the 7.1~pp mean within-strategy model gap---decoding strategy and model family contribute roughly equally to performance variance.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Four-class RF accuracy (\%) across the $3 \times 3$ atlas, with d1--d3 three-class accuracy in parentheses (chance = 25\% / 33\%). Depth-0 recall exceeds 98\% in all cells.}
\label{tab:main_matrix}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
& Nucleus & Temp.\ $\tau{=}0.9$ & Top-$k$ \\
\midrule
Pythia-1.4B  & 78.2\,(71.2) & 76.3\,(70.6) & 69.6\,(58.8) \\
OLMo-1B     & 78.8\,(75.0) & 82.0\,(76.3) & 74.2\,(66.1) \\
GPT-2~XL    & 83.3\,(79.0) & 85.4\,(82.6) & 76.6\,(69.5) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Per-class recall distribution.}
Depth-0 recall exceeds 98\% in all 9 cells, confirming that human-written text is trivially separable from any generation depth.
Among generated depths, d2 consistently yields the lowest recall (46--73\% across cells), followed by d3 (58--82\%) and d1 (72--91\%).
For example, Pythia-1.4B nucleus achieves per-class recall of d0$\,{=}\,$99\%, d1$\,{=}\,$82\%, d2$\,{=}\,$59\%, d3$\,{=}\,$72\%.
The strongest d2 recall is obtained by GPT-2~XL nucleus (73\%).
The d2 trough reflects its position at the center of the depth gradient: d2 features overlap with both the d1 distribution above and d3 below, making it the most confusable class---consistent with the d2-vs-d3 pair being the EDD bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
Full per-class recall for all cells appears in Appendix~\ref{app:per_class}.

%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Feature Consistency Across the Grid}
\label{sec:atlas:features}

Despite the 15.8~pp accuracy spread across cells, a small feature family dominates in every setting.
The 90th-percentile perplexity (\texttt{p90\_ppl}) ranks top-2 by Gini importance in all 9 cells; surprisal variance (\texttt{var\_surprisal}) in 7/9 (8/9 under SHAP; Appendix~\ref{app:permutation}).
Table~\ref{tab:feature_importance} shows the full per-cell ranking.

Cross-model feature-rank Spearman correlation averages $\bar{\rho} = 0.868$ (range $[0.619, 0.954]$): models agree on which features carry depth information even when they differ in absolute accuracy.
Among strategies, top-$k$ yields the highest cross-model rank correlation ($\rho = 0.811$)---the deterministic vocabulary truncation imposes a more uniform feature landscape across architectures, at the cost of weaker overall signal (\S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}).

Percentile-based features outperform their moment-based counterparts.
Token-level perplexity distributions are heavy-tailed: individual outlier passages can dominate the arithmetic mean of their depth class, whereas \texttt{p90\_ppl} is robust to such extremes while still capturing the tail erosion that signals generation depth.

Feature ablation confirms this concentration: the top-2 features (\texttt{p90\_ppl} + \texttt{var\_surprisal}) alone reach 91.1\% of full accuracy (71.5\%), and the top-5 features achieve 97.6\% (76.5\% vs.\ 78.4\%), with perplexity statistics alone reaching 76.6\% (vs.\ surprisal 73.2\%, other categories $<$46\%).
Variance inflation analysis reveals VIF${>}$10 for 14--16 of 19 features, placing the effective independent dimensionality at ${\approx}$4--5.
Forward selection independently confirms the dominant pair: \texttt{var\_surprisal} is selected first in 6/9 cells, \texttt{p90\_ppl} in 3/9.

The feature hierarchy also shifts with depth.
At shallow boundaries (d1 vs.\ d2), \texttt{var\_surprisal} dominates importance; at deeper boundaries (d3 vs.\ d4, d4 vs.\ d5), tail perplexity statistics (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) take over.
This transition aligns with model-collapse dynamics~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}: early recursion narrows the surprisal distribution (captured by its variance), while later steps erode the perplexity tail (captured by upper quantiles and kurtosis).
